title: UN Security Council adopts Resolution 2735 endorsing a Gaza ceasefire deal
body:
On 10 June 2024, the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 2735, which welcomed the three-phase ceasefire proposal announced by President Joe Biden on 31 May 2024. The resolution passed with 14 votes in favour; Russia abstained. It stated that Israel had accepted the deal and called on Hamas to accept it as well, urging both sides to implement its terms without delay and without condition.

Phase one provided for an immediate, full ceasefire, hostage releases including women, the elderly and the wounded, the return of some remains of deceased hostages, and a prisoner exchange. Israeli forces would withdraw from populated areas of Gaza, displaced Palestinians could return to their homes including in the north, and humanitarian aid would be distributed at scale. If negotiations on phase one exceeded six weeks, the ceasefire would continue as long as talks did.

Phase two would bring a permanent end to hostilities in exchange for the release of all remaining hostages and a full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza. Phase three would be a multi-year reconstruction plan and the return of any remaining deceased hostages. The resolution also rejected any demographic or territorial change in Gaza, reaffirmed support for a two-state solution and stressed the unification of Gaza with the West Bank under the Palestinian Authority. Algeria's ambassador, Amar Bendjama, said Algeria voted in favour to give diplomacy a chance.
